New machine. Its objects are: vesoso, mekukil, kanago, denasa, gumusu, vinatir.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to see how the machine responds.

TEST: vesoso, mekukil, kanago
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group didn't light up. That fits several possible rules. If any single nexiom lights the machine, then both nexioms are among the other three. If both nexioms must be present together, then they just aren't both in that first group. Testing the other half will help tell these apart.

TEST: denasa, gumusu, vinatir
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The second group lit up, so the nexioms' effect is in denasa, gumusu, vinatir. If one nexiom alone lights the machine, both are in that group. If both are needed together, they must also both be there, since splitting them would have left neither group lit. Either way the nexioms are two of these three. Testing denasa alone helps separate the possibilities and the two rules.

TEST: denasa
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Since non-nexioms never affect the machine, it can only respond to how many nexioms are present. An empty machine presumably stays dark, so 0 nexioms means no light.
- The first group stayed dark and the second lit up. One nexiom in each group would give the same count but different results, which is impossible. Both nexioms in the first group would leave the second group empty of nexioms, yet it lit. So both nexioms are in {denasa, gumusu, vinatir}, and having both present lights the machine.
- Denasa alone stayed dark. That leaves three candidate pairs: {denasa, gumusu}, {denasa, vinatir} or {gumusu, vinatir}. If denasa is a nexiom, one nexiom alone does not light the machine.

Testing gumusu + vinatir:
- If it lights up, the pair is {gumusu, vinatir}. A denasa pair would put only one nexiom there, and one alone doesn't light it.
- If it stays dark, the pair includes denasa. Then testing denasa + gumusu settles which one.

TEST: gumusu, vinatir
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Gumusu + vinatir stayed dark. Having both nexioms present lights the machine, so {gumusu, vinatir} is not the pair. That means denasa is a nexiom, and its partner is either gumusu or vinatir.

Testing denasa + gumusu settles it:
- If it lights up, the pair is {denasa, gumusu}.
- If it stays dark, the pair is {denasa, vinatir}.

TEST: denasa, gumusu
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Denasa + gumusu lit up, which happens only when both nexioms are present. This matches every earlier result:
- The first group (vesoso, mekukil, kanago) held no nexioms and stayed dark.
- The second group held both nexioms and lit up.
- Denasa alone and gumusu + vinatir each held only one nexiom and stayed dark.

So the machine appears to light only when both nexioms are on it together.

ANSWER: nexioms = denasa, gumusu
One last question. If only denasa were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. I tested denasa alone directly in my third test, and the machine did not light up. That fits the rule the tests point to: the machine lights only when both nexioms, denasa and gumusu, are on it together. A single nexiom is not enough.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: muvafi, bukuvis, digamok, kakubur, gukamor, vamenil.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to see how the machine responds.

TEST: muvafi, bukuvis, digamok
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first three objects did not light the machine, but I don't yet know the rule. If any single nexiom lights it, both nexioms must be among the other three. If both are needed together, they could be split between the groups. Testing the other three objects as a group will help separate these cases.

TEST: kakubur, gukamor, vamenil
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Since the first group did not light the machine and the second did, the nexioms are most likely both among kakubur, gukamor and vamenil. I still need to know whether one nexiom alone is enough to light the machine. Testing kakubur by itself will help with both questions.

TEST: kakubur
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

After three tests, three pairs are still possible:

- **One nexiom is enough:** the nexioms must be outside the first group and cannot include kakubur, so they would be gukamor and vamenil.
- **Both nexioms are needed together:** they must both be in the second group, so the pair is kakubur–gukamor, kakubur–vamenil or gukamor–vamenil.
- **Exactly one nexiom lights it:** this is ruled out. The first test needs zero or two nexioms in the first group. The second test needs exactly one in the second group. These cannot both hold.

So the candidates are {gukamor, vamenil}, {kakubur, vamenil} and {kakubur, gukamor}.

I'll test kakubur and vamenil together.
- If it lights up, the answer is {gukamor, vamenil} or {kakubur, vamenil}. Testing gukamor and vamenil next will tell them apart.
- If it does not light up, the answer is {kakubur, gukamor} or {gukamor, vamenil}. Testing gukamor and vamenil will also settle that.

TEST: kakubur, vamenil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The fourth test rules out two of the three remaining pairs:
- **{kakubur, vamenil}:** if both were nexioms and both are needed together, this test would have lit up.
- **{gukamor, vamenil} with one nexiom enough:** vamenil alone would have lit the machine.

Two possibilities remain, and both require the nexioms together:
- {kakubur, gukamor}
- {gukamor, vamenil}

Testing gukamor and vamenil together separates them. If it lights up, the nexioms are gukamor and vamenil. If it does not, they are kakubur and gukamor.

TEST: gukamor, vamenil
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The last test ruled out {gukamor, vamenil}: if both were nexioms and both are needed together, it would have lit up. That leaves one pair, which matches all five results if the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it:

- **Test 1 (muvafi, bukuvis, digamok):** neither nexiom present, so no light.
- **Test 2 (kakubur, gukamor, vamenil):** both nexioms present, so it lit up.
- **Test 3 (kakubur alone):** only one nexiom, so no light.
- **Test 4 (kakubur, vamenil):** only one nexiom, so no light.
- **Test 5 (gukamor, vamenil):** only one nexiom, so no light.

This assumes the machine follows a simple rule like "lights with at least one nexiom" or "lights only with both"; under those rules no other pair fits.

ANSWER: nexioms = kakubur, gukamor
One last question. If only gukamor were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

Probably not. My best explanation of the five results is that the machine lights only when both nexioms, kakubur and gukamor, are on it together. Under that rule, gukamor alone is just one nexiom, so the machine would stay dark.

I never actually tested gukamor by itself, so this is an inference, not an observation. It depends on the machine following a simple rule such as "lights with at least one nexiom" or "lights only with both." I ruled out "at least one" because kakubur alone did not light it, and I ruled out "exactly one" because it was inconsistent with the first two tests. A stranger rule, such as gukamor being enough on its own but cancelled out by vamenil, could fit the results differently. I can't rule that out with the tests I ran.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: mubupul, limurus, fokipen, sukoren, nifugi, meposik.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

I'll start by testing half of the objects to narrow down where the nexioms are.

TEST: mubupul, limurus, fokipen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first group didn't light, so next I'll test the other three objects. This helps narrow down both where the nexioms are and how the machine reacts to them.

TEST: sukoren, nifugi, meposik
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

Test 1 (mubupul, limurus, fokipen) stayed dark and test 2 (sukoren, nifugi, meposik) lit up. This points strongly to both nexioms being among sukoren, nifugi and meposik.

I don't yet know the machine's rule. It might light when any nexiom is present ("any"), or only when both are present ("both"). The rule "exactly one nexiom present" doesn't fit: it would need test 1 to hold zero or two nexioms and test 2 to hold one, which never adds up to two. So the possibilities are three pairs under two rules.

Testing sukoren and nifugi together lets me sort these out in the remaining tests:
- **If it stays dark:** the rule is "both" and the pair is sukoren+meposik or nifugi+meposik. Testing sukoren with meposik will settle it.
- **If it lights:** testing sukoren alone splits the possibilities.
  - If sukoren alone lights, the rule is "any" and the pair is sukoren+nifugi or sukoren+meposik. Testing nifugi alone decides.
  - If sukoren alone stays dark, the pair is nifugi+meposik ("any") or sukoren+nifugi ("both"). Testing nifugi alone decides that too.

TEST: sukoren, nifugi
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

The sukoren + nifugi test stayed dark. Under "any" it would have lit, because every remaining pair contains sukoren or nifugi. So the rule is "lights only when both nexioms are present."

With that rule, sukoren and nifugi are not the pair. The nexioms must be meposik plus either sukoren or nifugi. Testing sukoren with meposik decides it: if it lights, the pair is sukoren + meposik; if it stays dark, it is nifugi + meposik.

TEST: sukoren, meposik
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

Every test so far fits the rule "lights only when both nexioms are present," with the pair being **sukoren + meposik**:
- Test 1 (mubupul, limurus, fokipen) has neither, so it stayed dark.
- Test 2 (sukoren, nifugi, meposik) has both, so it lit.
- Test 3 (sukoren, nifugi) lacks meposik, so it stayed dark.
- Test 4 (sukoren, meposik) has both, so it lit.

One other rule also fits: "lights whenever meposik is present, and the other nexiom has no effect." I'll use my last test on meposik alone to check this.
- **If it stays dark:** the "both" rule is confirmed, and the answer is sukoren + meposik.
- **If it lights:** only meposik matters. Then I can't identify the second nexiom with no tests left.

TEST: meposik
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

Meposik alone stayed dark, which rules out "only meposik matters." The pair can also be read directly from the tests:
- Test 4 (sukoren, meposik) lit, but test 5 (meposik alone) did not. The only difference is sukoren, so sukoren must be a nexiom.
- Test 2 (sukoren, nifugi, meposik) lit, but test 3 (sukoren, nifugi) did not. The only difference is meposik, so meposik must be a nexiom.

All five results fit the rule "the machine lights only when both nexioms are present."

ANSWER: nexioms = sukoren, meposik
One last question. If only meposik were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

No. This exact setup was my fifth test: meposik alone stayed dark. That fits the rule the tests point to, where the machine lights only when both nexioms (sukoren and meposik) are on it together. Meposik by itself is not enough.

PROBE: no

New machine. Its objects are: tegofa, gizapas, rivoda, rasemen, norupen, ditilu.
You have 5 tests. Make your first move.

The rule is unknown: the machine might light when any nexiom is present, or only when both are. So I'll start by testing half of the objects.

TEST: tegofa, gizapas, rivoda
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 4 tests left. Make your next move.

The first test did not light up. If the machine lights when either nexiom is present, both nexioms are among rasemen, norupen and ditilu. If it needs both nexioms, the only thing ruled out is both being in tegofa, gizapas, rivoda. That leaves about 15 possibilities, so I want a test that splits them roughly in half.

Testing rasemen, norupen, tegofa and gizapas does that. Under the "either" rule it lights in all 3 remaining cases. Under the "both" rule it lights in 5 cases. That gives 8 cases where it lights and 7 where it doesn't.

TEST: rasemen, norupen, tegofa, gizapas
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 3 tests left. Make your next move.

The machine did not light in either test, so it cannot be lighting whenever any single nexiom is present. That rule would force both nexioms to be ditilu, which is impossible. It most likely lights only when both nexioms are on it together. Under that rule, 7 pairs remain:

- tegofa + ditilu
- gizapas + ditilu
- rivoda + rasemen
- rivoda + norupen
- rivoda + ditilu
- rasemen + ditilu
- norupen + ditilu

Testing ditilu, rivoda and rasemen splits these into 3 pairs that would light (rivoda + rasemen, rivoda + ditilu, rasemen + ditilu) and 4 that would not. Either outcome leaves few enough pairs to finish with the 2 tests after this one.

TEST: ditilu, rivoda, rasemen
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have 2 tests left. Make your next move.

Neither single-nexiom rule fits, so the machine most likely lights only when both nexioms are on it. Three tests without light leave 4 possible pairs:

- tegofa + ditilu
- gizapas + ditilu
- rivoda + norupen
- norupen + ditilu

Testing ditilu, tegofa and norupen splits these evenly. It would light for tegofa + ditilu and norupen + ditilu. It would stay dark for gizapas + ditilu and rivoda + norupen. My last test can then tell apart the two pairs that are left.

TEST: ditilu, tegofa, norupen
Result: the machine LIT UP. You have 1 test left. Make your next move.

The machine lit up, so the pair is now one of two:

- tegofa + ditilu
- norupen + ditilu

This assumes the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, which is the only rule I've found that fits all four results so far.

My last test is tegofa and ditilu alone. If it lights, the nexioms are tegofa and ditilu. If it doesn't, they are norupen and ditilu.

TEST: tegofa, ditilu
Result: the machine did NOT light up. You have used all your tests. Give your ANSWER now.

The tegofa and ditilu test did not light, so that pair is out. Under the rule that the machine lights only when both nexioms are on it, the remaining pair is norupen and ditilu. That pair fits all five results: the machine lit only in test 4, the one test that had both. Other, less likely rules could also fit, but this one explains everything I saw.

ANSWER: nexioms = norupen, ditilu
One last question. If only ditilu were on the machine, with nothing else, would it light up? End your message with one line: PROBE: yes or PROBE: no

**No**, I don't expect it to light. Every result fits the machine lighting only when both nexioms, norupen and ditilu, are on it together. Ditilu without norupen was tested twice, in test 3 (with rivoda and rasemen) and test 5 (with tegofa), and it stayed dark both times. On its own, ditilu should behave the same way.

I never tested ditilu alone, so this is inferred from the rule, not observed. It would only be wrong if the machine responded to an odd combination I haven't seen, such as ditilu alone lighting it while ditilu plus certain non-nexioms did not. That's unlikely, since non-nexioms never affect the machine.

PROBE: no
